question: Why is GSA5_surrogate at 72150 morphologies/cpu-h when GSA2_hetero (same lane, same budget in GSAB1) is at 354046 (4.91x)?

data.batch: GSAB1 (post-fix repair batch of the lane-arm sampler wiring defect)
data.aggregate_arm_stats_scope: GSAB1 seeds only (defective pre-fix GSA_* dispositions retained separately as scored artifacts)

one_stage_attribution: promotion-and-parent-allocation ranking stage (GSA5 rank=surrogate_allocation vs GSA2 rank=novelty)

factor_distinct_yield.definition: mean distinct_t2_viable_phenotypes GSA2 / GSA5 per seed (5062.7 / 2233.3)

factor_cpu_per_seed.definition: mean cpu_seconds GSA5 / GSA2 per seed (111.257 / 51.258)

decomposition.note: product of the two factors equals the rate ratio (rounding)

lane_composition.evidence: GSAB1 manifest pins GSA5 lane_weights {hetero: 1.0} — identical to GSA2_hetero; same seeded weighted_sampler

viability_funnel.evidence: T0 viable rate 0.7484 (GSA2) vs 0.7422 (GSA5); T1 and T2 gates pass 1.0000 in BOTH arms; per-seed tier-eval counts identical across arms (e.g. s0 T1=17123, T2=5802 in both) — SH schedule fixes eval counts and they match

evaluation_cost_per_genome.evidence: identical tier-eval counts per seed; the +60.0 cpu-s/seed delta is ranking machinery, not real evaluation (per-round cpu 1.75-1.91 s flat across 62 rounds for GSA5 vs ~0.8 s for GSA2)

mechanism.distinct_yield_loss: allocation_score = p_viable * max(0, predicted_t1_score) is a pure function of the ~120-dim grammar one-hot feature vector (surrogate_allocate.genome_feature_vector), so it cannot distinguish genomes sharing a feature vector and systematically re-promotes the incumbent high-scoring cells. The parent-pool refresh (search/successive_halving.py:230-233) sorts by the SAME rank_fn, and 80% of each cohort is mutation/crossover of those parents, making the collapse self-reinforcing. Novelty ranking diversifies both promotions and parents.
mechanism.cpu_overhead: 62 fresh EnsembleSurrogate retrains per seed (2 sklearn HistGradientBoosting fits on the round-local 531 T0 / 204 T1 records each) plus ~750 single-row sklearn predicts per round for rank_prepare = ~0.97 s/round = +60 s/seed on top of byte-matched real-eval work.

defects_named.where: search/surrogate_allocate.py:_StumpTree.predict (depth guard can return the internal-node float('nan') leaf marker set in _build)
defects_named.observed: holdout_mae_t1 = NaN in 5/6 GSA5 seeds, degenerate 0.0 in s2
defects_named.impact: the ONLY validation statistic of the surrogate was never usable on-host; surrogate ranking quality went unmeasured. Ranking itself unaffected in the sklearn path (stumps are used only for the holdout MAE).

not_a_defect: lane_weights: correctly pinned {hetero: 1.0} for GSA5 in GSAB1 (the earlier sampler-wiring defect, named by worker N, is repaired and retained)

round-local surrogate training (n_train_t0=531, n_train_t1=204 per round, never cumulative) is a frozen design choice, not wiring; it caps the surrogate at <=729 examples/round and is a plausible revival lever
relation_to_frozen_terminal: The read explains the GSA5 residual INSIDE MORPHOLOGY_SEARCH_COST_DOMINATES__SWEEP (ranking-machinery cost + allocation-induced redundancy), does not re-litigate it.
revival_levers_not_executed: novelty-gated surrogate allocation (surrogate proposes, novelty disposes) to break duplicate promotion
batch-row sklearn predicts + cumulative-round training to cut the 2.17x CPU factor
dedup-by-phenotype_digest at promotion so T2 budget cannot be spent on already-survived phenotypes
